ag.start.lead: Say it in your own words: a ready-made app, your GitHub project, or something you want built. The agent proposes, you approve each step.
ag.start.manual: Start from a file or a repository instead
ag.start.note: Nothing is created on your Liara account until you approve it, and every price is shown first.

ag.waiting_card: The approval is at the top of the page, with the price and the buttons.
agt.auto: Apply code fixes to Launchpad's copy without asking
agt.auto_d: Your own files are never changed, and every change is shown as a diff afterwards. Anything that costs money is always asked.
agt.d: Connect Claude Code, Cursor or another agent that speaks MCP. It can fix your real repository when a deploy fails because of your code, and with the deploy permission it can take a project from a Git repository to a running app without you copying anything.
agt.deploy: Let this agent deploy for me
agt.deploy_d: It can add a project, start a deployment, answer its questions, supply secrets and approve the plan, including its price. It can never delete anything. Leave it off and the token only reads and fixes code.
agt.name: Name
al.d: Launchpad checks every 5 minutes that your running apps still answer. If one stops answering, it can send you a short chat message, and another when it is back. To get them, paste a webhook link: a link from a chat app that receives messages. In Discord: Edit channel, Integrations, Webhooks, New webhook, Copy URL. Slack and Mattermost incoming webhooks work too. If you leave this empty, nothing is sent; you still see the status on the project page.
al.set: An alert address is set. It is stored encrypted and not shown again.
ann.fix: Approval needed for a fix. {title} {price} Choose Apply or Decline. It expires in {minutes} minutes.
ann.handoff: The run is waiting for your own coding agent. Connect it with the command on the screen.
ann.interrupted: The run was interrupted when the server restarted. Its log is still readable.
ann.live: Finished. {project} is live at {url}. {passed} of {total} checks passed.
ann.plan: Approval needed. {title} {price}Nothing is created until you choose Apply. Decline stops the run. It expires in {minutes} minutes.
ann.plan_price: About {hourly} toman per hour, {monthly} per month, VAT included.
ann.question: The agent has a question. {text} Choices: {options}.
ann.removed: Removed from Liara. Nothing from this run is running or billed.
ann.secret: The agent needs the value of {name}. Type it in the password field and press Send. It is sent once and never stored.
ann.sent.question: Your answer was sent.
ann.sent.secret: The value was sent. It is not stored.
ap.blockers: {count} blockers: nothing can be created until you fix them.
ap.created_note: The resources created so far keep billing while we decide.
ap.decline_fix: If you decline, the run stops here. What was created stays up and keeps billing (about {hourly}/hour) until you delete it.
ap.decline_plan: Declining stops the run and nothing is created. If nobody answers in {minutes} minutes it counts as a no. We only change things we created; your other apps are never touched.
ap.delta_note: I only show the difference. The new price comes back from Liara after the change.
ap.disk_note: The disk is not in this total because its price is unverified.
ap.expired: This request expired and was declined safely. Nothing was approved.
ap.gone: That request is no longer waiting. The page has been refreshed.
ap.included: included or billed separately, not verified
ap.secret_note: It is sent once. It is not kept on this page, not put in the address and not written to any log.

ask.wait.d: The run continues as soon as you answer. Nothing is created before that.

auth.register.title: Create an account
auth.to_login: Already have an account? Sign in

br.d: Deploy another branch of this repository as its own project, with its own app and database, to try a change before it reaches the main one. It costs like any other app until you delete it.
br.name: Branch
cf.a.d: Launchpad reads the error, changes the code in its own copy, deploys again and checks the app.
cf.a.none: Launchpad has no automatic fix for this error, and no AI model is connected.
cf.a.p1: Your own files are never touched
cf.a.p2: Every change is shown as a diff
cf.a.p3: Afterwards you can send the fix to your repository as a pull request
cf.b.d: Connect Claude Code, Cursor or any agent that speaks MCP to Launchpad. It reads this error, fixes your real code and tells Launchpad to continue.
cf.b.p1: Nothing to copy between the two tools
cf.b.p2: Works on your own repository and in your own editor
cf.b.p3: The same run continues and checks the app
cf.b.t: Fix it with my own agent
cf.note: Anything that costs money or changes your running app still needs your approval here.
cf.remember: Remember my choice for this project
cfs.d: Who fixes it for this project. A run asks the first time; you can keep the answer here.

chat.card.create_from_git: Download {url} and make it a project
chat.card.install_ready_made: Create the project {name} that installs the ready-made app {app}
chat.card.label: Proposed change
chat.card.redeploy: Release the newest code of {project} from its repository
chat.card.start_run_preview: Look at {project} and show what would be created (nothing is created)
chat.d.general: Tell it what you want: look at a project, start one from a GitHub repository, or install a ready-made app.
chat.d.project: Ask about this project or tell it what to change. Changes only happen after you press a button.
chat.decide_first: Decide on the proposed change above first.
chat.empty.general: Not sure where to start? Try one of these, or write your own.
chat.empty.project: Try one of these, or write your own.
chat.hidden: Something you wrote looked like a secret, so it was hidden before the assistant saw it.
chat.idea.diagnose: My site shows an error or is slow: find out why
chat.idea.gen.repo: Deploy one of my GitHub repositories
chat.idea.versions: Go back to the previous version
chat.never: Never type passwords or keys here. When one is needed, a private box appears on the card.
chat.off: The assistant cannot reach its AI model right now.
chat.ph.general: Describe what you want to do…
chat.ph.label: Message to the assistant
chat.ph.project: Ask something or describe a change…
chat.price.down: Costs about {n} toman less per month (with VAT)
chat.price.up: Costs about {n} toman more per month (with VAT)
chat.tool.create_project_from_git: Downloaded the repository as a project
chat.tool.install_ready_made: Made a project for the ready-made app
chat.value.note: Goes straight to Liara. The assistant never sees it and it is not stored here.
chat.warn.approve_each: You still approve each thing it creates, on the run page.
chat.warn.build_minutes: The build takes a few minutes. Ask afterwards how it went.
chat.warn.deploy_quota: Liara allows {cap} releases a day for this app and {used} were made in the last 24 hours: only a few are left.
chat.warn.dns_records: You then add the DNS records it shows you at your domain's registrar.
chat.warn.edit_local: Saved only in this server's copy of the project. Nothing is online until you release it.
chat.warn.edit_not_in_repo: Your Git repository is not changed. Copy the changes there too, or a redeploy from the repository drops them.
chat.warn.irreversible: Databases, disks and files are deleted for good. This cannot be undone.
chat.warn.nothing_created: Nothing is created on Liara yet. You review the plan and its price on the project's page first.
chat.warn.nothing_new: Nothing new is created and no setting changes.
chat.warn.rebuild: A new release is built from the old code and the app restarts.
chat.warn.restart: The app restarts so it can use the change.
chat.warn.restart_brief: The app restarts, so it is unreachable for a short moment.
clean.lead: This deletes the apps and databases this run created, and nothing else. Type the project name to confirm.
clean.title: Delete what this run created
connect.lang.lead: Sets the interface and the language of the notes and questions the AI writes.
connect.lang.title: Language of the agent
connect.lead: I deploy to your own Liara account, so I need an API token from it. We only ever modify apps and databases we created ourselves. Your existing apps are never touched.
connect.sees: I can see on your account
connect.sees.why: Seeing your apps lets me stop before I reuse a name. I never change them.
connect.step1: Open the Liara console and go to the API page.
connect.step2: Create a new token. Name it something you will recognise, such as "Liara Launchpad".
connect.step3: Copy it. Liara shows it only once.
connect.step4: Paste it below and press Check token. I do not save anything until you press Save.
connect.stored: The token is stored encrypted and never shown again.
connect.team.label: Team
connect.team.q: Which team should I deploy to?
connect.team.why: Your account belongs to teams. Until you choose one, I cannot see which apps exist, so I would not notice a name clash. I will not guess.
connect.title: Connect your Liara account
connect.token.hint: The token stays in this field until you save. It is never put in the address bar.
cost.derived: A month is counted as 720 hours.
cost.fix_delta: The fix changed the price by {delta}/hour.
dash.agent.d: Describe it in your own words. The agent finds the app, uses your GitHub project, or builds what you describe, and asks you before it creates anything.
dash.agent.t: Tell the agent what you want to deploy
dash.card.cost.note: VAT included. Only resources this tool created are counted.
dash.card.live.noexp: The free address ends 7 days after the first deploy.
dash.card.live.one: {name} answers at its free address, which stops working in {n} days.
dash.card.wait.many: These runs are waiting for you. Nothing is created until you answer.
dash.card.wait.one: {name} is waiting for your approval. Nothing is created until you answer; it expires in {t}.
dash.empty.lead: Tell me what you want online, or give me your project. I tell you what it needs and what it costs, and wait for your yes. Nothing is created or billed before that.
dash.error: The projects could not be loaded.
dash.lead: Everything you have given me, and what it is doing on your Liara account right now.
dash.new.manual: Deploy a zip or Git repo
dash.or: Or start from your own files
dash.start.git.d: A public repository, or a private one once GitHub is connected.
dash.start.rm.d: WordPress, n8n, Ghost and more, installed for you.
dash.start.zip.d: A .zip of your project. Secret files such as .env are never uploaded.

demo.apply_note: Demo: the sample ends at the approval. After Apply, the deploy events of the dry-run sample are replayed so you can review the working and live states.
demo.banner: Demo: a recorded run replayed in the page, with no backend and nothing sent anywhere.
diag.advice.a_little_slow: The site answered in {ms} ms: acceptable, but on the slow side.
diag.advice.cpu_tight: CPU peaked at {peak_percent}% of the plan.
diag.advice.memory_tight: Memory peaked at {peak_percent}% of the plan. A busier day could push it over the limit.
diag.ai.ask: Ask the AI to look deeper
diag.ai.asking: The AI is reading the logs…
diag.ai.none: The AI had nothing more to say from this evidence.
diag.ai.note: The AI only reads: it changes nothing.
diag.ai.t: The AI's reading (a second opinion, lower confidence)
diag.ai.ungrounded: No line of the log backs this up: treat it as a guess.
diag.ask: The assistant can make these changes for you: ask it in the chat on a run's page.
diag.auto: Found automatically when the site stopped answering
diag.cause.bad_release: The newest release is the first suspect
diag.cause.bad_release.d: A release went out {minutes} minutes ago and the site has been failing since.
diag.cause.bound_to_localhost.d: Liara's router cannot reach an app that is bound to localhost.
diag.cause.code_error.d: The logs hold an exception that the app does not handle.
diag.cause.cpu_saturated.d: CPU reached {peak_percent}% of the plan while the site was slow or failing.
diag.cause.db_auth_failed.d: The user name or password the app uses is not accepted.
diag.cause.db_localhost: The app looks for its database on localhost
diag.cause.db_localhost.d: On Liara the database is a separate service with its own address.
diag.cause.errors_in_logs: The site answers, but errors are logged
diag.cause.memory_exhausted: Memory is at the plan's limit
diag.cause.memory_exhausted.d: Memory reached {peak_percent}% of the {ram_gb} GB the plan gives. Past the limit the app is killed and restarted, and the site shows errors.
diag.cause.missing_env.d: The app asks for {names}, which is not set.
diag.cause.missing_node_module.d: The code requires {module}, which is not in package.json.
diag.cause.missing_python_module.d: The code imports {module}, which is not in the dependencies.
diag.cause.not_serving.d: It answers {http} and nothing in the logs says why.
diag.cause.out_of_memory: The app ran out of memory
diag.cause.out_of_memory.d: The process was killed or stopped because it needed more memory than the plan gives.
diag.cause.outbound_blocked: The app cannot reach an outside service
diag.cause.outbound_blocked.d: Calls to another service are refused from Liara's servers.
diag.cause.release_unhealthy: The current release is not healthy
diag.cause.slow_response: The site is slow, and no resource is short
diag.cause.slow_response.d: It answered in {ms} ms while CPU and memory are fine, so the time goes inside the code.
diag.cause.still_starting.d: It is {minutes} minutes old and nothing in the logs is wrong. Some apps need several minutes on their first start.
diag.cause.wrong_port: The app listens on another port
diag.cause.wrong_port.d: The port Liara sends traffic to is not the one the app opened.
diag.d: Probes the site, reads the logs, releases, CPU and memory, and ranks what is most likely wrong.
diag.fix.check_port_and_bind: Check that the app listens on the configured port, on 0.0.0.0.
diag.fix.fix_code: Read the file the error points to, fix it, and release the edit.
diag.fix.optimise_cpu: Find the slow request or loop, or choose a bigger plan.
diag.fix.profile: Look for slow database queries, calls to other services, or work done on every request; add caching.
diag.fix.read_logs: Read the logs around the first error.
diag.fix.reduce_memory: Reduce what the app keeps in memory, or choose a bigger plan.
diag.fix.resize_plan: Move to a bigger plan (restarts the app).
diag.fix.rollback: Go back to the release before it (Deployments tab, "Go back to this version").
diag.fix.wait: Give it a few minutes and check again.
diag.none: No problem found: the site answers quickly and nothing is wrong in the logs, memory or CPU.
diag.rechecking: Done. Checking the result in a moment…
dom.badge.cert.help: The free SSL certificate. REQUESTING means Liara is issuing it; it usually takes a minute or two. Press Check records to refresh.
dom.badge.domain.help: The domain's own status at Liara. ACTIVE means Liara found your DNS records and the domain is connected to the app.
dom.check.busy: Liara is already checking. Try again in a minute.
dom.check.sent: Asked Liara to check the nameservers.
dom.console: Open the domain page in the Liara console
dom.d: Connect a domain you own so your app has a permanent address. The free liara.run address stops working after 7 days.
dom.derived.help: Liara's API does not give this value, so the agent worked it out. Compare it with the Liara console before you rely on it.
dom.detach.elsewhere: Your DNS records at your DNS provider stay. Remove them there too if you no longer need them.
dom.detach.records: Also remove the {n} DNS records Liara added for it from your Liara DNS zone {zone}. Your own records are not touched.
dom.detach.removed: The domain was removed, and {n} DNS records were removed from your Liara DNS zone.
dom.dns.error: Could not run the DNS check. Try again in a moment.
dom.dns.v.all_good: The nameservers and every public resolver return the right records.
dom.dns.v.missing: Your zone's nameservers ({ns}) do not return one of the records. Add it at your DNS provider or in your Liara DNS zone.
dom.dns.v.no_nameservers: The domain has no nameservers that anyone can find. It may not be registered, or its nameservers are not set yet at the registrar.
dom.dns.v.not_at_liara: The domain's nameservers ({ns}) are not Liara's, so records kept in a Liara DNS zone are not served. Either set Liara's nameservers at your registrar, or add the records where the domain's DNS really is.
dom.dns.v.not_at_liara.t: The domain does not use Liara's nameservers
dom.dns.v.propagating: The records are right at the nameservers, but some resolvers still remember the old answer. This fixes itself, usually within an hour. Nothing is wrong.
dom.dns.v.unknown: The nameservers did not answer in time. Try again in a moment.
dom.dns.v.wrong_value: A record exists but its value is not the one Liara asks for. Compare it with the records above.
dom.dns.v.wrong_value.t: A record points to the wrong place
dom.mode.lbl: Where is the domain's DNS managed?
dom.mode.liara: On Liara (Liara adds the records itself; I change the nameservers once)
dom.mode.own: At my registrar or another DNS provider (I add the records myself)
dom.ns.d: At the place you bought {zone}, replace its nameservers with these. It can take a while before this takes effect.
dom.plan.attached: This domain is already attached to the app. Connecting only reads it again.
dom.rec.status.help: Liara's check of this record: VALID means it found it at your DNS provider, INVALID means it did not.
dom.record_status: See which record Liara has verified (in the Liara console)
dom.records.d: Add these at your DNS provider. Names are relative to your domain. Then press Check records.
dom.records.none: The records are not shown here. Open the domain page in the Liara console to see them.
dom.ssl.sent: Requested. The certificate can take a minute to appear.
dom.ssl.wait: Available once the records are in place.
dom.suggested.help: Liara's answer did not name this record. It is shown for you to compare with the Liara console, and the agent never adds it for you.
dom.unmanaged: This domain was added outside the agent, so it is shown for reference only.
dom.value.console: The value is in the Liara console.
dom.wait.d: DNS changes spread slowly: usually a few minutes, sometimes an hour or more. Until then your domain may not open or may show an error, and your own computer may remember the old answer for a while. Your free liara.run address keeps working in the meantime. Press Check records now and then. You do not need to do anything else.
dom.wait.t: A new domain takes a while to start working
dom.www: Also attach www and redirect it to this domain
dom.zone.d: Only needed when the zone is not the last two parts of the domain, for example for a domain under a company-owned name.
err.action_invalid: That change could not be applied (it was already decided, a value is missing, or the name typed does not match).
err.action_pending: Decide on the proposed change first.
err.bad_credentials: The username or the password is wrong.
err.bad_mode: That run mode is not supported.
err.bad_option: That is not one of the offered answers.
err.bad_payload: The request body is not valid.
err.bad_username: The username must be 3 to 32 characters: a-z, 0-9, underscore, dot or hyphen.
err.bad_zip: This is not a valid .zip file.
err.chat_busy: The assistant is still answering. Wait a moment.
err.chat_full: This conversation is full. Clear it to start again.
err.cleanup_failed: The cleanup did not finish. A database that is still being set up cannot be deleted yet: wait until Liara shows it as running, then try again. Nothing else was touched.
err.confirm_mismatch: The name you typed does not match.
err.csrf: The request was blocked for safety. Reload the page and try again.
err.deploy_limit_reached: This app has used its releases for the day ({used} of {cap} on the {tier} tier). That is Liara's limit: wait for it to reset or move to a higher tier.
err.domain_invalid: That is not a domain name. Use something like mydomain.com.
err.domain_is_liara_address: That is Liara's free address. Connect a domain you own.
err.domain_not_found: That domain is not attached to this app.
err.domain_taken: That domain is already attached to an app on Liara.
err.git_branch: That is not a valid branch name.
err.git_credentials: Remove the username and password from the address. For a private repository use the access token field.
err.git_failed: I could not download this repository. Check that it exists and is public.
err.git_host: {host} is not allowed. Use one of: {allowed}.
err.git_missing: Git is not available on the server. Upload a .zip instead.
err.git_path: The address should look like https://github.com/owner/repo.
err.git_scheme: Use an address that starts with https://.
err.git_timeout: Downloading took too long. Try again, or upload a .zip.
err.git_token_invalid: That does not look like an access token.
err.github_no_write: The token cannot write to this repository. It needs the repo scope, or Contents and Pull requests write access.
err.github_not_found: GitHub does not show that repository to this token.
err.github_oauth_failed: GitHub did not complete the sign-in.
err.github_oauth_off: Login with GitHub is not set up on this server.
err.github_oauth_state: This sign-in was not started from here. Try connecting again.
err.github_token_rejected: GitHub did not accept the access token.
err.invite_required: This server needs a valid invite code to create an account.
err.liara_forbidden: Liara refused this token (HTTP {status}). It may not have the permission this needs.
err.liara_token_invalid: Liara did not accept your API token (HTTP {status}). Check it in the Liara console.
err.liara_unreachable: Liara could not be reached. Try again in a moment.
err.llm_empty: The AI model gave no answer. Try again.
err.llm_failed: The AI model could not be reached. Try again in a moment.
err.llm_unavailable: The AI model is not set up on this server.
err.network: The server could not be reached. Check your connection and try again.
err.no_live_app: Deploy the project first. A domain needs a running app.
err.no_such_request: That question is no longer waiting. It may have expired.
err.not_a_git_project: Only a project that came from a Git repository can preview a branch.
err.not_found: That does not exist, or it is not yours.
err.not_owned: This agent did not create that, so it will not change it.
err.nothing_to_explain: There is nothing in the log to explain yet.
err.oneclick_needs_vm: This app needs a cloud server, which this agent does not create.
err.oneclick_unknown: That is not one of Liara's ready-made apps.
err.path_traversal: The zip has a file path that points outside the project, so I rejected it.
err.pr_bad_path: The changes name a file outside the project.
err.pr_needs_token: An access token that can write to the repository is needed.
err.pr_no_patch: The agent made no changes to this project.
err.pr_not_github: Pull requests can only be opened on GitHub repositories.
err.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.
err.release_current: That release is already the running one.
err.release_not_found: That release is not in this app's history.
err.release_not_ready: Only a release that was running fine can be rolled back to.
err.rollback_unavailable: This release cannot be rolled back to.
err.run_active: A run is already active for this project.
err.source_required: Upload a .zip file or paste a Git address.
err.symlink: The zip contains symbolic links, which are not allowed.
err.too_large: The project is larger than {limit_mb} MB once unpacked.
err.too_many_files: The project has more than {limit} files.
err.too_many_runs: You already have the maximum number of active runs.
err.upload_too_large: The file is larger than {limit_mb} MB.
err.validation: Some of the values are not valid.
err.weak_password: The password needs at least 8 characters.
err.webhook_credentials: Do not put a user name or password in the address.
err.webhook_failed: The address did not accept the message.
err.webhook_private: That address points inside a private network, which is not allowed.
err.webhook_scheme: The address must start with https://.
err.webhook_unresolved: That host could not be found.
err.wp_bad_host: That is not a valid host or port.
err.wp_busy: An upload is already running for this project.
err.wp_ftp_refused: The FTPS server refused a file.
err.wp_ftp_unreachable: Could not talk to the FTPS server. Check the host, the port and implicit or explicit mode.
err.wp_host_private: That host points inside a private network, which is not allowed.
err.wp_host_unresolved: That host could not be found.
err.wp_login_failed: The FTPS server refused the user name or password.
err.wp_no_content: This project has no wp-content folder.
err.wp_nothing_to_send: There are no theme, plugin or language files to send.
err.wp_tls_failed: The server's security certificate could not be verified.
err.wp_too_large: There are too many or too large files to send from here.
explain.note: Written by an AI model from the last lines of the log, with secrets hidden. It can be wrong: check it against the log.
fail.banner: The resources created so far are billing while we decide.
fail.banner_sub: You can delete them any time with the button above; nothing else on your account is touched.
fb.d: Launchpad changed {files} in its own copy to make the app run. Without the same change in your repository, the next deploy from it fails the same way.
fb.t: The fix has to go back to your code
files.none_sub: If I change a copy of one of your files, the diff shows here and I ask first.
fp.d: The agent changed your code to make it run. Apply this patch to your repository with git apply.
gh.d: Connect your GitHub account to download private repositories without pasting a token, and to send the agent's fixes as a pull request. It asks for the repo permission. You can disconnect at any time.
gh.new.d: Connect GitHub once to pick any of your repositories, private ones included, without pasting a token. You can disconnect at any time.
gh.pick: Or pick one of your repositories
ho.call.redeploy: Your agent asked for a new deploy
ho.call.wait_for_run: Your agent is following the run
ho.note: If nobody answers within 30 minutes, the run stops and reports the error.
ho.nothing_yet: Waiting for your agent to connect…
ho.s2: 2. Tell your agent what to do
ho.sakoo: Stop waiting, let Launchpad fix it
ho.title: Your own agent is fixing the code
ho.token_hint: It lets your agent read your projects and send code fixes. It cannot delete anything or spend money.
ho.token_once: The token is inside the command below. It is shown only now, so copy it.
home.connect.lead: Nothing can be deployed until an account is connected.

land.ask.go.anon: Sign up and tell the agent
land.ask.label: What do you want to deploy?
land.ask.manual: Have your own files? Upload a zip or give a Git address
land.ask.ph: e.g. Put WordPress online for my blog
land.cta.anon: Connect your Liara account to continue
land.drop.title: Drop a .zip here
land.go.h: Ready to put your project online?
land.go.p: Tell the agent what you want, or start with a zip file or a Git link. It takes a few minutes.
land.h1: Tell the agent. It deploys to Liara.
land.lead: Say what you want online in your own words: WordPress for a blog, n8n, your GitHub project, or a small app it builds for you. It lists what it will create on your Liara account with prices, and creates nothing until you approve.
land.led.note: A disk is shown with no price: whether it is included or billed separately is not verified. Moving an app from basic to silver is priced as a difference: +306 toman/hour, +220,002 toman/month.
land.login: Already have an account? Sign in
land.lp.alt: An animation: a project drops onto a glowing platform, its language and database are recognised, and a live address appears.
land.mcp.0.p: Give it a Git repository or one of Liara's ready-made apps. It starts the deploy, reads the plan and its price, and answers what the run asks.
land.mcp.1.p: When the code breaks the deploy it gets the cause, the file and the line, fixes your repository on your machine and pushes. Secrets are filtered out before it sees any log.
land.mcp.2.h: It follows it until it is healthy
land.mcp.2.p: It watches the run until your app answers. Spending money needs the exact price repeated back, and only a token you marked as allowed to deploy can approve at all.
land.mcp.note: Your agent can never delete anything, change a price, or touch domains or tokens, and no Liara or Git credential ever goes through MCP.
land.nav.label: Sections
land.net.alt: The private network of the sample run, with the connections between its resources and the price of each one:
land.net.note: The disk has no price yet: Liara has not said whether it is inside the plan or billed separately.
land.s1.p: The sheet on the left replays the same sample run as you scroll. Each step below is an event the agent really emits.
land.s2.p: Apps and databases are created with the plan and tier shown in the approval. Figures below are from the sample run.
land.s3.p: You stay in charge from the first click to the last.
land.s4.h: Already use a coding agent? Plug it in.
land.s4.p: Connect Claude Code, Cursor or any agent that speaks MCP. Your agent can take a project from a Git repository to a running app, and when a deploy fails because of your code it reads the error, fixes your real repository and tells Launchpad to continue. Nothing to copy and paste.
land.sheet.title: Replay of a sample run
land.src: Replay of the sample events. Figures and names are the sample's, not a quote for your project.
land.step.0.p: It opens the zip or clones the repository and looks for manifests. Each decision keeps the file it came from.
land.step.1.p: It chooses apps, databases and disks. It asks only when the files do not answer, for example a worker with no port.
land.step.2.p: It stops at an approval that shows the total per hour and per month, VAT included. Nothing exists on your account yet.
land.step.3.p: It creates one resource at a time, then requests the URL. If a build fails it diagnoses the cause. A fix that costs money waits for you.
land.title: Liara Launchpad · Deploy to Liara
land.toolnote.anon: Not connected. Nothing is created until you approve a plan.
land.toolnote.authed: Nothing is created until you approve a plan.
land.w.title_net: The private network net1: each resource joins it when it is created
land.w.title_replay: Replay: the agent reads a project, draws the plan with prices, waits for approval, then creates and verifies the resources
land.why.fix.p: If something goes wrong, it finds out why and tries to put it right. It asks you before anything that costs money.
land.why.own.p: It works only inside your own Liara account. Your passwords and keys stay hidden, always.
land.why.price.p: You see the cost per hour and per month up front, taxes included. No surprises later.
land.why.yes.p: It shows you what it plans and waits. Until you say yes, nothing is created.

lim.daily: Releases in the last 24 hours: {used} of {cap} (the {tier} tier)
lim.daily.note: An estimate: Liara does not document how it counts the day. A release past the cap is refused by Liara with HTTP 428.
lim.daily.unlimited: Releases in the last 24 hours: {used} (this tier has no daily cap)
lim.known.app_names_global: Use a taken app name: names are unique across all of Liara, so the agent picks a free one.
lim.known.cpu_unit_unknown: Be sure of the CPU unit: Liara does not document it, so it is read as cores.
lim.known.daily_deployments: Release an app more times a day than its tier allows (basic 20, silver 50, gold unlimited).
lim.known.free_address_expires: Keep the free liara.run address past 7 days: a custom domain is needed.
lim.known.logs_lag: Show logs and charts instantly: they trail the app by some seconds, and are empty until the container has started.
lim.known.networks_not_deletable: Delete a private network: an empty one stays until you remove it in the Liara console.
lim.known.release_not_cancellable: Cancel a release that is building: stopping a run stops the agent, and Liara finishes the build.
lim.known.t: What the agent cannot do, because Liara's API has no call for it
lim.known.tier_fixed_at_creation: Change the feature tier (basic, silver, gold) of an existing app: that means creating the app again.

reg.step.irnic_enter_ns: In «نام کارگزار» (name server) enter Liara's name servers, one per row: {nameservers}. Up to four rows are allowed.
reg.step.irnic_enter_own_ns: Enter the name servers of the company that hosts your DNS (its panel shows them), one per row.
reg.step.irnic_ip_empty: Leave the IP field empty: it is only for name servers under your own domain.
reg.step.irnic_login: Sign in to IRNIC's panel at {url} with your NIC handle (شناسه کاربری) and password.
reg.step.irnic_secret: Type the answer to your security question («پاسخ سؤال امنیتی»).
reg.step.ns_pending: Liara's name servers show up once the domain is connected to Liara's DNS: connect it first, then come back to this list.
reg.step.records_at_provider: At your DNS provider add the {count} records listed above for {domain}.
reg.step.reg_find_ns: Find the domain's name server (NS or DNS) settings.
reg.step.reg_login: Sign in to the panel of the company where you bought the domain.
reg.step.reg_own_ns: Make sure the name servers are those of the company that hosts your DNS.
reg.step.reg_set_ns: Replace the name servers with Liara's, one per row: {nameservers}.
reg.step.verify: Then press «Check DNS» above, or ask the assistant to check it.
reg.step.wait: The change spreads in minutes, sometimes up to 72 hours (.ir domains can be slow). You can close this page.
rel.confirm: Deploy this version again? Liara creates a new release from it. Your environment variables, database and domains stay as they are.
rel.d: Every release of this app on Liara. If a new version breaks, go back to an earlier one that worked.
rel.done: Rolled back. The app answers again.
rel.done_unchecked: Rolled back, but the app did not answer yet. Give it a minute and check the address.
rel.failed: The rollback did not finish (state {state}). Look at the app's logs in the Liara console.
rel.via_image: The agent did not deploy this release, so Liara's own saved image of it is used. That route is less certain than a kept source.
res.next.t: What you still need to do
rm.d: Open-source apps Liara lists for one-click install, such as n8n or Ghost. Installing one here starts a normal run: you see the plan and its cost first, and nothing is created until you approve it. The app is deployed from its ready-made image with the sizes the app recommends.
rm.link: Or install a ready-made app (n8n, Ghost and others)
rm.text: Nothing from this run is running on your Liara account any more. The history below is only a record.
rm.title: Ready-made apps
rm.vm: Needs a cloud server (not created by this agent)

run.sub.buildfailed: The build did not finish. What I found, and what I can do about it, is below.
run.sub.cancelled: Nothing was created and nothing is billed. You can run it again any time.
run.sub.failed: I could not finish this run. What I know is below.
run.sub.fix: This costs more, so it is your call.
run.sub.interrupted: The server restarted while this run was going. The log below is what happened up to then.
run.sub.live: I opened the address myself and it answered.
run.sub.preview: This was a dry run: nothing was sent to Liara and nothing was created.
run.sub.question: The files do not answer this, and I will not guess.
run.sub.reading: I am looking at your files. Nothing is created.
run.sub.removed: Everything this run created was deleted. Nothing is running and nothing is billed. The run stays below as a record.
run.sub.secret: It is sent once and never shown again.
run.sub.stopped: Nothing more will be created. Anything created before you stopped is still on your Liara account: delete it from here if you don't want it.
run.sub.thinking: I decide what Liara needs and what it costs. Nothing is created yet.
run.sub.waiting: Here's what I'll create. Nothing happens until you approve.
run.sub.working: One at a time, then I check the address.

wp.after: Next, in the console: import your database dump with phpMyAdmin (Database tab), and if pages show permission errors use the file manager's automatic permission fix. Then close the FTPS access.
wp.d: For a managed WordPress site you already made in the console: its files go in over FTPS, the way Liara's own guides describe. WordPress itself stays as Liara installed it, and wp-config.php is never touched. Starting from nothing? Start a run for this project and choose to install WordPress through the API: the agent then creates the site and sends these files itself, with no console steps.
wp.implicit: Implicit FTPS (port 990). Leave off for the usual explicit FTPS (port 21)
wp.never: The password is used for this transfer and is not stored. Existing files with the same name are replaced. The database is not part of this.
wp.plan: {n} files ({mb} MB) from {parts} will be sent.
wp.s1: In the console, open your WordPress site:
wp.s2: Go to FTPS, then Create FTPS access. Copy the host, port, user and password it shows.
wp.t: Send your WordPress code to a Liara WordPress site
wp.uploads: Also send the uploads folder (pictures and media, can be large)
